Extreme heat and manual labor may drive violence, particularly against women and children, due to economic stress, poor livelihoods, and institutional vulnerabilities.

Global research also links extreme heat to higher rates of interpersonal violence, with studies suggesting a 4.49% increase in intimate partner violence prevalence for every 1°C rise in temperature.

**Why it Matters:**
This trend has significant implications for public health, social welfare, and crime prevention in Bangladesh and other countries with similar climate conditions.
